en: Vulcan Point is a tiny island holding a crater lake inside the main crater lake of Taal Volcano.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly into the sea, meaning its lower half is affected by ocean tides.
Mount Hamiguitan features a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees grow only a few feet tall due to harsh conditions.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site located entirely in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by hand over 2,000 years ago without modern equipment.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous worldwide for having the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone shape on Earth.
The Sibuyan Sea is often called the Galapagos of Asia because it contains unique, untouched marine and island ecosystems.
The massive Pearl of Lao Tzu, one of the largest natural pearls ever found, was discovered in the waters of Palawan.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds formed from ancient coral deposits uplifted by tectonic activity.
The Philippines is a central part of the Coral Triangle, an ocean area containing the highest diversity of marine life globally.
The Agusan Marsh in Mindanao is the largest freshwater swamp forest in the Philippines and a crucial habitat for migratory birds.
The Philippine Trench is one of the deepest ocean trenches in the world, plunging to a depth of over 10,000 meters.
